title: Tarrasch Defense: the ideas
line: Black strikes at the center at once and gets open lines for every piece.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares too. It holds the center.

also.g8f6: That is the start of the Indian defenses, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.after: White offers a side pawn to pull your center pawn away. This is the Queen's Gambit.

steps.text: Guard the center pawn with the pawn in front of your king.

also.c7c6: That is the Slav Defense, also sound. This lesson guards with the king pawn.
also.d5c4: That is the Queen's Gambit Accepted, also sound. This lesson keeps the center pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c7 two squares. It strikes at White's center pawn at once.

also.g8f6: That is the Queen's Gambit Declined, also sound. This lesson strikes at the center.
also.f8e7: That is a calm Queen's Gambit Declined, also sound. This lesson strikes at the center.
also.c7c6: That heads for the Semi-Slav, also sound. This lesson strikes at the center.

steps.after: This is the Tarrasch Defense. White trades on d5.

steps.text: Take back with the king pawn. Your bishop on c8 now has an open diagonal.

also.c5d4: That is the Schara Gambit, a sharp choice. This lesson takes back on d5.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It adds pressure on the pawn on d4.
steps.after: White takes the pawn on c5. It looks like a free pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on d5 one square. It chases the knight on c3 away from the center.
steps.after: The knight goes to the edge of the board.

steps.text: Take the pawn back with the bishop. Material is level again.
steps.after: The knight takes your bishop. You have a check that takes it back.

steps.text: Check with the queen. It also attacks the knight on c5.
Take the knight. That makes up for your bishop.
steps.after: Material is level. Black has a big pawn in the center and open lines for its pieces.

summary: Black strikes at the center at once. The pawns open up, and Black gets free play for all its pieces.
